<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this work we focus on Weyl's class, a simple yet algebraically general class of solutions of static, axisymmetric geometries. Employing the canonical forms of rank-2 Killing tensors, we systematically derive, for all separable coordinate systems at once, the constraints that must be satisfied for these spacetimes to admit genuine hidden symmetries. Our analysis yields an analytical characterization of the obstructions to integrability within subclasses of Weyl's class, both in vacuum and electro-vacuum. In particular, we find that no two-Killing-vector member of Weyl's class in vacuum admits an irreducible Killing tensor capable of supplying the additional integral of motion required for complete integrability, with Schwarzschild being the only exception. In electro-vacuum, the same holds for charged particles when the Killing tensor is aligned with the electromagnetic field, with Reissner-Nordstr"om as the only exception. As a matter of fact, members of Weyl's class admitting a third Killing-vector isometry (i.e. Levi-Civita) are already completely integrable through their manifest symmetries alone, and an explicit integration of the Killing equations shows that they admit only reducible Killing tensors. This result provides an analytic complement to previous analytical and numerical investigations, and establishes a systematic connection between the absence of hidden symmetries and the absence of quadratic integrals beyond the isometries. Beyond the specific classification obtained here, these results demonstrate the potential of our approach regarding the canonical forms of Killing tensor as a systematic tool for probing hidden symmetries in Petrov type I spacetimes.</jats:p>
